sections.what: The Harm Reduction Action Center is a fiscally sponsored Denver project offering naloxone, safer-use supplies and a low-barrier drop-in space. Its staff provide overdose-response training and connect visitors with health and social services. A city presentation says the project serves more than 4,000 people annually, but that figure is not a verified count of unique opioid-risk clients. The modeled N=4,000 is a rounded historical service proxy rather than a matched audited cohort. A monthly 797-client count and convenience-sample survey are not annualized. Exact expense-to-cohort matching remains unverified.
sections.monitoring: Original DDPHE 2023 SAP needs assessment PDF pp13-16 describes 946 respondents, 923 retained, convenience recruitment at HRAC and Access Point, uneven recruitment protocols and a 25-dollar incentive. It pools sites and records housing status rather than county residence. Thus it cannot supply HRAC annual unique reach, a representative HRAC opioid exposure fraction, or MSA attribution. Its drug-use factsheet explicitly does not account for concurrent drugs. August 2026 contract exhibit p8 contains targets, not completed outputs. ARPA period runs January 2024 through September 2026, OAF January through December 2026. Do not annualize the ARPA target, add overlapping people across funding streams, or turn kits into deaths averted. Both streams include third-party kit recipients.
sections.qualitative: Model one overdose-mortality pathway as Q_local=N*k*p*r*L*b*g. Only the service proxy and accounting costs have direct source anchors. k=.5, conditional p=.03, r=.1, L=10, b=.4 and g=.95 are judgments. At these settings the scenario implies six deaths averted before funding attribution, 2.4 after it and 2.28 local, or 22.8 local QALYs. Neither kits nor reported reversals are equated with prevented deaths. Other benefits are unquantified, not demonstrated zero; the result is not a lower bound.
sections.cost: FY2024 HRAC whole sponsored-project accounting expense is $2,017,429, including $266,735 intercompany support, recorded in-kind program resources, personal assistance and event costs. The audited combining schedule supplies project-specific detail. No additional sponsor gross-up or current fee is added. This is observed accounting cost, not a verified complete economic opportunity-cost denominator. Medical in-kind wholesale valuation, unrecorded volunteer work and external partner inputs retain uncertainty. FY2025 project expense is $1,884,959 and is used only as cost sensitivity because matched 2025 reach is unverified. Contract service location is City and County of Denver. Service eligibility/location is not client residence. Retain g=.95 only as judgment within OMB-23-01 Denver-Aurora-Centennial MSA, excluding Boulder, Greeley and Colorado Springs.
sections.funding: Organization says gifts support service expansion, naloxone and supplies and its drop-in site. It does not give a priced incremental staff shift, unique cohort, stockout, or match opportunity. Denver adopted resolution 26-1273 on August 31, 2026. The third amendment changes ARPA scope to operations and retains OAF building-purchase language in the legislative title; no agreement capacity or term increase. The attached exhibit mixes procurement-of-facility labeling with operating services. It cannot be used as a clean whole-project annual budget. Exhibit A-03 p7 prints ARPA 489376 and OAF 239345 (sum 728721), while the earlier amended agreement total was 968127 and April's increase was 239375. Preserve this discrepancy; do not silently correct the exhibit or sum its numbers as the current full agreement amount. These are HRAC project columns, unlike sponsor-wide reserves. Restricted net assets may include ordinary project-purpose restrictions and are not necessarily locked capital; the schedules do not split individual donor restrictions. Neither cash nor a 149-dollar unrestricted balance alone establishes liquidity crisis, spare capacity, or additionality. b=.4 remains unsupported scenario judgment. Public naloxone support, other local providers and the new operating grant use create substitution questions; state June 2025 award maintained free naloxone through June 2026 but does not establish September 2026 availability at HRAC. Official donation page links https://acefzmsz.donorsupport.co/-/XCYYADTX; direct audit retrieval returned HTTP 404, so checkout success is unverified.

model.geographicAttribution: HRAC explicitly serves Denver people who inject drugs, with Denver fixed/mobile services. g=.95 is a judged recipient residence share within OMB-23-01 Denver-Aurora-Centennial MSA, not a measured address distribution. model.counterfactual: Without HRAC, clients may access other syringe programs, public naloxone and EMS. r is incremental recipient efficacy beyond substitutes; b is the share of modeled activity attributable to incremental funding. Neither is measured.

inputs.name: p
inputs.rationale: Judged 3% annual fatal-overdose risk conditional on the k=.5 subgroup, not across every service recipient.

inputs.name: r
inputs.rationale: Judged 10% recipient mortality reduction beyond substitute naloxone/EMS/services; not calibrated from a recipient trial.

inputs.name: L
inputs.rationale: Judged ten discounted quality-adjusted remaining years per death averted; recipient survival and utility unmeasured.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Judged .4 funding additionality; public grant resources and existing supply may substitute for new gifts. A deficit alone is not a funding gap.

sensitivity: Poor/favorable jointly vary conditional risk, causal conversion, utility/duration, additionality and geography; not confidence intervals.
Halving local attribution or doubling cost doubles price; zero additionality gives no finite price.
All-client and 54/137 primary-preference scenarios are denominator illustrations, not measured opioid exposure.
2025 expense changes cost only; historical service proxy does not establish a matched 2025 cohort.
No further sponsor-fee gross-up or recorded in-kind addition is valid without a reconciled resource allocation.
